Your Snake game is ready — `snake_zai-glm-5.3_01.html` (603 lines, single self-contained file: HTML + CSS + JavaScript).

**What's inside:**

- **30×30 grid** on a 600×600 canvas, classic continuous movement (~110 ms per tick) in four directions
- **Core rules** — eating food grows the snake and adds a point; hitting a wall, your own body, or the other snake ends the game
- **Three modes** (chosen from the start menu):
  - `1` — Human vs Human (P1: arrow keys · P2: WASD)
  - `2` — CPU vs Human (human uses arrows **or** WASD)
  - `3` — CPU vs CPU (watch the AI battle)

- **Live HUD** — scores for both snakes (green vs blue) and the current mode shown above the board during play
- **Start menu** — title screen with clickable mode buttons and key hints
- **Game over screen** — result (winner / draw), final scores, restart options
- **Restart with a keypress** — `R`, `Enter`, or `Space` restarts the same mode instantly; `M` returns to the menu; `P` pauses mid-game

Extras: simultaneous head-on collisions kill both snakes, the food never spawns on a snake, rounded snake segments with directional eyes, glowing food, and arrow/space key presses are `preventDefault`-ed so the page never scrolls.

Just open the file in any browser and press `1`, `2`, or `3` to play.

{"edit_description":"Create a NEW complete single-file HTML5 Snake game (HTML + CSS + JS inline, no external assets) at this path. Spec:

LAYOUT/STYLE: Dark theme (#0f172a background, lighter panel colors). Centered column: title "SNAKE", a HUD bar showing both snakes' scores with colored chips, then a 600x600 <canvas id="board"> wrapped in a relatively-positioned container, plus two absolutely-positioned overlay divs (#menu-overlay, #gameover-overlay) covering the canvas with semi-transparent backdrops and centered panels. Clean modern look, rounded corners, subtle shadows. Monospace/sans font stack.

CONSTANTS: GRID=30, CELL=20, TICK_MS=110.

GAME MODES (selected from start menu): 'hh' human vs human, 'ch' cpu vs human, 'cc' cpu vs cpu. Menu lists three clickable buttons labeled "1 — Human vs Human" (P1: arrow keys, P2: WASD), "2 — CPU vs Human" (you: arrows or WASD vs CPU), "3 — CPU vs CPU" (watch AI vs AI). Keys 1/2/3 also start the corresponding mode directly.

SNAKES: Each snake = {body: array of {x,y} head-first, dir:{x,y}, nextDir, color, name, score, cpu, alive}. Snake 1 ("Green", #22c55e) spawns body [(5,15),(6,15),(7,15)] heading right. Snake 2 ("Blue", #3b82f6) spawns body [(24,14),(23,14),(22,14)] heading left. In 'ch' mode the human controls snake 1 and BOTH arrow keys and WASD steer it; snake 2 is CPU. In 'hh' arrows steer snake 1, WASD steer snake 2. In 'cc' both are CPU.

INPUT: Single keydown listener on window. preventDefault for arrows/space always. Direction input validated: ignore if opposite of current dir or same as current dir (queue via nextDir applied at tick start). 'p' toggles pause during play. On game over screen: 'r', Enter or Space restarts the same mode; 'm' returns to the menu.

FOOD: Single food {x,y}, spawned on a random cell not occupied by any snake, drawn as a red glowing circle. When a snake head lands on food: score++, snake grows (tail NOT removed that tick), food respawns on a new free cell.

TICK LOGIC (both snakes move every tick, deaths evaluated simultaneously before anyone is removed): compute newHead = head + dir for each alive snake. A snake dies if newHead is out of bounds (wall), hits its own body cells (excluding its own tail cell only if that snake is not eating this tick), hits the other snake's body cells (excluding the other's tail cell only if the other is not eating this tick), head-to-head (both newHeads equal), or head swap (newHead of A equals B's head while B's newHead equals A's head). Apply deaths; surviving-but-both-moved snakes then advance; eating snakes grow. Game ends immediately when any snake dies (both may die the same tick). On game over: winner = the surviving snake if exactly one died; if both died same tick, higher score wins, equal scores = "Draw". Show result, both final scores, and hints "R — play again · M — menu".

CPU AI (function chooseCpuDir(snake, other, food)): blocked cells = every cell of both snakes' bodies EXCEPT each snake's tail-tip cell (tails vacate). 1) BFS from snake head to food over free cells; if a path exists, take the first step as nextDir (never reverse into own neck). 2) Fallback: consider the 3 non-reverse directions; keep only in-bounds, non-blocked ones; score each candidate by flood-fill count of reachable free cells from that candidate cell (iterative flood fill, cap ~400 cells) + small bonus if it reduces Manhattan distance to food; pick the best. 3) If nothing is safe, keep current dir.

GAME LOOP: requestAnimationFrame with time accumulator so tick cadence is exact and pause is trivial. state machine: 'menu' | 'playing' | 'paused' | 'gameover'. Restarting clears all state (interval-free), resets snakes/scores/food.

RENDERING (every frame): canvas background, faint grid lines (rgba white ~0.04), food circle with glow, snake segments as rounded rects with slight darker outline; head drawn brighter with two small eye dots offset by current direction; dead snakes flash red for ~300ms before overlay appears (or just draw normally and show overlay — keep simple but the eyes and rounded segments are required). HUD updates every frame: colored dot + name + score for each snake plus mode name; also a small "P — pause" hint.

Make the code clean vanilla JS (no libraries), all in one <script> at the end of <body>, with small helper functions. Ensure no console errors and that menu/game-over overlays toggle correctly via a .hidden {display:none} class.","path":"snake_zai-glm-5.3_01.html"}
